statements.claim: Krishna came to the war riding Garuda, the king of birds and enemy of serpents, who crosses the sky swifter than wind, and went to Indra in the etherial region where he blew his conch Panchajanya, increasing the fear of the Daityas.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (Dutt): 'the deity Hari came there riding on Garuda, the enemy of the serpents... went to Sakra in the etherial region (2). Coming near Vasava, the lord Krishna duly blew the conch Panchajunya which increased the fear of the Daityas'; pack locations: 'sky over city Vajra'.

statements.claim: Pradyumna, hearing the conch, came to his father Keshava, who told him 'Speedily kill Vajranabha' and then 'Go there on Garuda's back'; saluting Indra and Krishna, Pradyumna mounted Garuda and went.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244: 'Hearing that sound Pradyumna... came near His father Keshava who said to him "Speedily kill Vajraalbha"... "Go there on Garuda's back". Saluting the foremost of celestials Indra and Upendra he did so.' (Upendra = Krishna; the story reads this as saluting Indra and his father.)

statements.claim: Seated firmly on Garuda, the heroic Pradyumna, well read in the use of all weapons, struck Vajranabha, wounding him on the breast with a club; Vajranabha lost consciousness and, bewildered like one dead, vomited blood again and again.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244: 'the heroic Pradyumna, well read in the use of all weapons, struck Vajranabha... wounded on the breast with a club... lost consciousness; and bewildered like one dead he vomitted blood again and again.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna, irrepressible in battle, told the fallen Vajranabha 'Be consoled', and Vajranabha, regaining consciousness, praised him — 'Well done, mighty Yadava; by your prowess you have become an illustrious enemy of mine; now is the time for me to strike you in return; wait here firmly.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (10-11): 'Thereat Krishna's son, irrepressible in battle, told him "Be consoled"... "Well done! Oh highly powerful Yadava. By your prowess you have become an illustrious enemy of mine. Now is the time for me to strike you in return; wait here firmly."'

statements.claim: Roaring like a hundred clouds, Vajranabha hurled a huge club adorned with bells, which struck Pradyumna on the forehead; Pradyumna vomited blood and lost consciousness.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (12-13): 'roaring like a hundred clouds the king of Daityas discharged... a huge club adorned with bells... wounded sorely on his forehead with that club... Pradyumna, vomitted blood and lost his conciousness.'

statements.claim: Seeing his son fall, Krishna blew his Panchajanya conch 'as if consoling his son', and at its sound Pradyumna revived and stood up.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (14): 'Seeing it the divine Krishna, the slayer of his enemies, blew his Panchajanya conch as if consoling his son. At the sound of that Panchanjanya... the highly powerful Pradyumna revived and stood up.'

statements.claim: Beholding Pradyumna revived, all the worlds were delighted — especially Indra and Krishna.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (15): 'beholding Pradyumna consoled, all the worlds especially Indra and Keshava were greatly delighted.'

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the conch blast made the air hold still, the Daityas 'remembered what followed it', and Pradyumna waited for the sound 'the way a son waits for his father's voice in a crowd'.
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing and imagery around the source's events; no factual assertion requiring a source.

notes: Close paraphrase of Harivamsha 1.244 (Dutt). Every narrative beat — Garuda ride, Panchajanya blast, 'Be consoled' exchange, club wound, conch revival, universal delight — matches the passage. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Recap: both warriors had been struck down and both had risen — Vajranabha from the breast wound, Pradyumna from the forehead blow, revived by his father's conch.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (same passage in pack): Vajranabha wounded on the breast then revived; Pradyumna wounded on the forehead, revived by Panchajanya.

statements.claim: Recap of the prior event: Pradyumna had ridden against the asura host with the serpent Ananta yoked to his celestial car, devastating their ranks while Indra sent his own car, his elephant Airavata and his son Jayanta to aid the Yadavas.
statements.evidence: Prior canonical event per corpus chain (DKS_0310): 'Pradyumna creates a celestial car with the thousand-headed serpent Ananta as charioteer and devastates the Asura host, while Indra sends his own car, Airavata and Jayanta to aid the Yadavas.'

statements.claim: According to Krishna's desire, his discus — set with thousands of sharpened axles and destructive of the Daityas — came through the air into his son's hand.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (16): 'according to Krishna's desire his discus, set with thousands of sharpened axles and destructive of the Daityas, came into the hand of his son.'

statements.claim: Saluting Indra and Krishna, Pradyumna discharged the discus, which separated Vajranabha's head from his body before the very presence of the Daityas.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (16-18): 'Saluting the high souled Indra and Upendra he discharged it... that discus, discharged by Narayana's son, separated Vajranabha's head from his body before the very presence of the Daityas.'

statements.claim: Sunabha, dreadful and taking delight in battle, was killed by Gada on the battlefield although he was very careful.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (19): 'The dreadful Sunabha, bent upon killing his enemies and taking delight in battles, was killed by Gada in the battle-field although he was very careful.'

statements.claim: Shamba, the aggrandiser of his enemies, with sharpened arrows sent the remaining enemies of the immortals into the family of Yama — i.e., despatched them.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (20): 'With sharpened arrows Shamva, the aggrandiser of his enemies, converted... the enemies of the immortals into the family members of Yama.'

statements.claim: Nikumbha, after Vajranabha's destruction, fled in fear of Narayana to the far city of Shatpura.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (21): 'After the destruction of the great Asura Vajranabha, Nikumbha, in fear of Narayana, fled to the city of Shatpura.'

statements.claim: Krishna and Indra came down to the city of Vajra, consoled the boys and old persons stricken with fear, and established peace there.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (22-23): 'the two high-souled Haris came down to the city of Vajra... Having consoled the boys and old persons stricken with fear those two foremost of celestials established peace there.'

statements.claim: Atmosphere/reflection: the pause before the discus, the sky imagery, and the closing thought that the young warrior 'began to understand what it meant to be trusted with such a weapon'.
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing around supported events.

notes: Faithful retelling of Harivamsha 1.244 (the discus slaying, Gada/Shamba/Nikumbha coda, and descent to pacify Vajra). No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Recap: Vajranabha was dead, slain by the discus in Pradyumna's hand; his army scattered; Nikumbha had fled to the far city of Shatpura; the boys and old people of Vajra had been consoled by Krishna and Indra.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (16-23): discus severs Vajranabha's head; Nikumbha flees to Shatpura; the two Haris come down to Vajra, console boys and old persons, establish peace.

statements.claim: Following Brihaspati's advice, Indra and Krishna consulted together about the present and the future and divided Vajranabha's conquered kingdom into four parts.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (24): 'following Vrihaspati's advice and consulting (with him) about the present and future (arrangements) the highly powerful and great Indra and Upendra divided Vajranabha's kingdom into four parts.'

statements.claim: The kingdom was divided into four parts: one fourth to Jayanta's son Vijaya, one fourth to Pradyumna's son, one fourth to Shamba's son, and the remaining fourth to Gada's son Chandraprabha.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (25-26): 'one-fourth of that kingdom, gained by conquest, was given to Jayanta's son Vijaya, one-fourth to Pradyumna's son, one-fourth to Shamva's son and the remaining one-fourth to Gada's son Chandraprabha.'

statements.claim: Vijaya, the son of Indra's son Jayanta, was a boy of the divine line who could already range through the upper (etherial) region.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (31): 'Vijaya, from before, could range in the etherial region.'

statements.claim: The four koti villages and one thousand prosperous branch cities like the town of Vajra were divided into four parts, as were warm clothing, deerskins, cloths and jewels, and Indra and Krishna took pleasure in giving it all away.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (27-28): 'with great pleasure Sakra and Keshava divided into four parts also the four koti villages and one thousand prosperous branch cities like the town of Vajra... also divided, into four parts, various warm clothings, deer-skin, cloths and jewels.'

statements.claim: Before the assembled Rishis, Indra and Krishna anointed the four young kings, pouring the water of the Ganga that issues from Vishnu's feet, with the music of celestial bugles.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (29-30): 'those heroic kings... were annointed there before the Rishis by the gods Sakra and Krishna with the water of Ganga issuing from Vishnu's feet, accompanied with the music of celestial bugles.'

statements.claim: Madhava's (Krishna's) descendants learned to range the etherial region through virtues inherited from their mothers, and would travel by the etherial way between the celestial region and Dwaraka, the city protected by the Bhaimas.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (31 and Indra's speech): 'Madhava's descendants, on account of the virtues inherited from their mother, practised it also'; 'They will acquire practice of going to the celestial region and Dwaraka protected by the Bhaimas through the etherial way.'

statements.claim: Indra told Jayanta: 'O heroic victor of armies, it behoves you to protect all these kings. One of them is a perpetuator of my race, the other three are born in the family of Keshava. By my command none amongst creatures will be able to kill them. Give them elephants born of the quarter-elephants, horses from the race of Ucchaisrava, and chariots built by the celestial architect.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.244 (Indra's speech, as rendered in pack): 'O heroic victor of armies, it behoves you to protect all these kings... one is a perpetuator of my race and the other three are born in the family of Keshava. By my command none amongst creatures will be able to kill them... Give them... elephants born from those of the quarter, horses born from the race of Ucchaisrava and chariots constructed by the celestial Arch[itect].'

statements.claim: Reflection: 'four shares are still one realm under a single protection', and the four young kings receive what they did not have to win.
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing; the underlying facts (division into four, Indra's protection) are supported.

notes: Faithful to Harivamsha 1.244 (24-31 + Indra's speech to Jayanta). All four recipients, the shares, the division of villages/cities/goods, the anointing, and Indra's boon match the passage. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Recap: Naraka, the son of the earth (Bhumi), had been slain; the maidens kept in his inner apartments were freed; the summit of Mount Mani had been uprooted and brought; the riches collected. Krishna told the Yadavas 'You are the masters of all these things', and the Bhojas, Andhakas and Vrishnis, their hair standing erect in joy, worshipped him.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.248 (Dutt): 'by virtue of your ascetic power... Bhumi's son Naraka has been slain. Many beautiful maidens have been released from his inner appartment and the summit of the mount Mani has been uprooted and brought here... You are now the masters of all these things... the Bhojas, Andhakas and Vrishnis, having their hairs stand erect in joy, worshipped Janarddana.'

statements.claim: The wives of the Dasharhas and of Ahuka came to the hall; the seven queens of Vasudeva, headed by Devaki and the beautiful-faced Rohini, saw Balarama and Krishna seated at ease.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.248 (7-8): 'the wives of the Dasharhas and Ahuka, filled with joy, repaired to the Hail for seeing Krishna. The seven queens of Vasudeva, headed by Devaki and the beautiful-faced Rohini saw the large-armed Rama and Krishna seated at ease.'

statements.claim: First the queens saluted Rohini, then Balarama and Krishna rose and saluted Devaki; the goddess shone among her two lotus-eyed sons as Aditi, mother of the gods, shines among Mitra and Varuna.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.248 (9-10): 'Having saluted first Rohini Rama and Krishna afterwards saluted Devaki. As Aditi, the mother of gods, looks beautiful in the company of Mitra and Varuna so the goddess shone in the company of her two lotus-eyed-sons.'

statements.claim: The illusory daughter of Yashoda — born at the very same moment as Krishna, and for whose sake he slew Kamsa with his relatives — appeared before Krishna and Balarama.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.248 (11-13): 'the illusory daughter of Yashoda, whom the people describe as one and without any parts, with whom... Krishna... was born at the same moment and for whom he slew Kansa with his relatives, appeared before Krishna and Rama.'

statements.claim: Until then she had been adored in the Vrishni family and brought up and maintained like a daughter; known to the world as the irrepressible Yoga maiden, one and without parts, born for the protection of Keshava, whom she guarded with her goddess-like celestial body, the Yadavas worshipped her with joy.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.248 (13-14): 'Up to this time she was being adored in the Vrishni family and was being brought up and maintained like a daughter. She, whom the people of the world know as the irrepressible Yoga maiden... was born for the protection of Keshava. Because she protected Keshava with her goddess-like celestial body the Yadavas used to worship her with great pleasure.'

statements.claim: Krishna approached her as a man goes to a beloved female friend and held her by the hand; Balarama also held her hand, embraced her and smelt her head.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.248 (16-17): 'Madhava approached her, like unto a man his beloved female friend and held her by the hand. The highly powerful Rama too held her by his right hand, embraced her and smelt her head.'

statements.claim: The Vrishni women saw her standing between her two brothers Balarama and Krishna, like the goddess Shree with golden lotuses in her hands seated on a lotus, showered her with fried paddy and flowers, and returned to their quarters.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.248 (18-19): 'The Vrishni women then saw her between her two brothers Rama and Krishna like unto the goddess Sree, with golden lotuses in her hands and seated on a lotus too. They then showered fried paddy and diverse flowers and repaired to their respective quarters.'

statements.claim: The Yadavas spent that time praising Krishna's wonders and honoring him, and Madhava, the enhancer of the joy of the citizens, lived on happily among his people.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.248 (20-21): 'speaking highly of the wonderful deeds of Janarddana and honoring him the Yadavas sat delightedly... Madhava, the enhancer of the joy of the citizens, began to live there happily with them.'

statements.claim: Soon after, the sage Narada came to the meeting at the order of the king of the gods, ready to tell the assembled Vrishnis the story of Krishna's boyhood — 'another telling'.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.248 (22-25): 'the worshipful saint Narada, according to the order of the king of gods, came to Janarddana at the meeting... said to the Vrishnis... hear now of all the heroic deeds which Krishna... has performed from his boyhood.'

statements.claim: Scene-setting: the women of the hall fell quiet as she passed and 'some of them had not seen her since she was a child'; the hall watched in silence.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric embellishment not asserted in the pack (the pack instead stresses she was brought up within the Vrishni family); vague, non-sourceable framing of the reunion.

notes: Faithful to Harivamsha 1.248 (Narada Describes the Feat of Krishna): Naraka recap, the queens' visit, Rohini/Devaki salutations, Yogamaya's appearance, Krishna and Balarama's greeting, the Shree simile, and Narada's arrival all match. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Kama (Cupid) of firm vows, to kill Shamvara, took birth from Rukmini — the incarnation of Lakshmi — and Vasudeva as their beautiful son Pradyumna.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (2): 'Kama (Cupid) of firm vows, in order to kill Shamvara, took his birth from Rukshmini, the incarnation of Lakshmi, and Vasudeva as his beautiful son Pradyumna.'

statements.claim: On the seventh day at dead of night Shamvara stole the week-old infant from the lying-in room and carried him to his own city; Krishna, who followed celestial Maya, knew everything and did not kill the Danava at that time.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (3-4): 'On the seventh day at dead of night Kalashamvara stole away that infant son of Krishna from the lying-in room... Krishna, who followed the celestial Maya, knew every thing and therefore he did not kill at that time the Danava... As if urged on by Death the great Asura stole away Krishna's son... took him to his own city.'

statements.claim: Shamvara had no children, and he gave the stolen baby to his wife Mayavati as though he were her own son.
statements.evidence: The pack (HV 1.251, 5-7) states the childless one was Mayavati — 'His beautiful and accomplished wife Mayavati... had no offspring so that Danava... gave over that son of Vasudeva to her like his own' — and the same Harivamsha account (1.252; DKS_0316/0317 packs) has Shamvara send his hundred sons against Pradyumna, so Shamvara was not childless.

statements.claim: Mayavati, seeing the infant, was filled with joy, her hair stood erect, and she gazed at him repeatedly with delight, recollecting that in a life before this one he had been her favourite husband — Kama, reduced to ashes long ago by the trident-bearing god (Shiva) stricken with sorrow for Sati.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (8-11): 'Seeing him she was filled with joy and her hairs stood erect: she looked at him repeatedly with delight... she recollected that he was her favourite husband... He was formerly reduced to ashes by the divine trident handed deity stricken with sorrow for Sati. Now he has been seen by me in another birth.'

statements.claim: Thinking 'being his wife and knowing him as my husband, how can I give him milk and address him as my son?', Mayavati handed the baby to a nurse; informed by the nurse, Pradyumna grew up believing Mayavati was his mother.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (12-14): '"However, being his wife and knowing him as my husband how can I give him milk and address him as my son?"... Mayavati handed over the baby to the nurse and soon reared him up... Informed by the nurse and out of ignorance Rukshmini's son knew Mayavati as his mother.'

statements.claim: Mayavati instructed the growing boy in all forms of illusion; he became a young man of striking beauty, an expert in the use of all sorts of weapons and quick to read those around him.
statements.evidence: Mostly HV 1.251 (15-16): she 'instructed him in all forms of illusion'; he 'looked highly beautiful, became an expert in the use of all sorts of weapons'. The closing clause generalizes the source's narrower 'in deciphering the movements of women' into 'quick to read the hidden intentions of the people around him' — a loose paraphrase, not a material distortion.

statements.claim: Mayavati, assuming the semblance of a beautiful woman, tempted him with her gestures; Pradyumna drew back, asking why she cast off a mother's feeling and behaved perversely — 'Women's minds flicker like lightning. Am I not your son? Tell me the secret of what you are doing.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (16-23): 'Mayavati, assuming the semblance of a beautiful woman, sought the company of her beloved consort and tempted him with her gestures... "Why do you, casting off your maternal feelings, behave in this perverse way?... The nature of women is fickle like lightning... Am I not then your son?... I wish to learn the secret of this from you."'

statements.claim: In a solitary place Mayavati revealed: 'You are not my son, and Shamvara is not your father. You are the son of Vasudeva and Rukmini, a prince of the Vrishnis. On your seventh night, when you were a helpless baby in the lying-in chamber, my husband stole you away.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (24-29): '"You are not my son, nor Shamvara is your father... you are the delightful son of Vasudeva and Rukshmini. After your birth on the seventh day you were brought here. When you were a helpless baby in the lying-in chamber you were stolen by my powerful husband."'

statements.claim: Mayavati told him his mother mourns him 'like a cow separated from her calf', and his father — mightier than Indra (Shakra), with the emblem of Garuda on his flag — does not even know he is alive; and she sought him as her lover because she did not give birth to him.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (28-33): 'Stricken with sorrow for a son like you your mother is bewailing like a cow estranged from its calf... your father, having the emblem of Garuda on his flag, and more powerful than even Shakra himself, does not know it... I seek you as my lover, because I have not given birth to you.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna, who had mastered all forms of illusion, was worked up with anger and resolved: 'Shall I cower here, afraid of the wretch who stole the infant son of Keshava? I will do what makes him angry — I will break his standard and call him out; when he comes to meet me I will kill him in battle and return to Dwaraka.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (34-38): 'Pradyumna... had mastered all forms of illusion. So... worked up with anger, he... called Shamvara. He said: "Alas shall I remain here fearing that wicked-souled Danava who has stolen away the infant son of Keshava? How may that sinful wretch become angry?... I should do what excites his anger... I will strike down the wonderful standard... If he comes to know of the spoliation of his standard Shamvara will surely come out. I will then kill him in battle and return to Dwaraka."'

statements.claim: Frame: 'the boy who was called Shamvara's son had believed it all his life... Both were lies, and the night he learned the truth, the lying ended in fire.'
statements.evidence: Metaphorical framing of the supported revelation scene; no factual assertion.

corrections.original_sentence: Shamvara had no children, and he gave the stolen baby to his wife Mayavati as though he were her own son.
corrections.suggested: Mayavati had no children of her own, and Shamvara gave the stolen baby to his wife as though he were her son.

notes: One CONTRADICTED: the story transfers the childlessness to Shamvara ('Shamvara had no children'), whereas the pack (HV 1.251) says it was Mayavati who had no offspring — and the same source has Shamvara send his hundred sons against Pradyumna (HV 1.252; corpus chain). Everything else — the theft on the seventh night, Mayavati's recognition of Kama, the confession, and Pradyumna's resolve — is faithful.

statements.claim: Recap: Pradyumna had come to Shamvara's city as a stolen child, carried out of Dwaraka on his seventh night, and had been raised as a prince of the demon house; Mayavati had just told him he was the son of Vasudeva and Rukmini.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (2-7, 24-33) as given in the pack: the infant stolen from the lying-in room on the seventh day and reared in Shamvara's city; Mayavati's confession that he is Vasudeva and Rukshmini's son. Corpus chain previous title confirms.

statements.claim: Pradyumna resolved not to slip away secretly but to provoke Shamvara into an open fight: 'I will strike down the wonderful standard at his gate, the jeweled standard with the lion, standing like Mount Sumeru itself. When Shamvara learns that his banner lies broken, he will come out to me. I will kill him in battle, and I will go home.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251: 'With my sharpened spear I will strike down the wonderful standard with a flying pennon having the emblem of a lion which stands like the mount Sumeru on his gate. If he comes to know of the spoliation of his standard Shamvara will surely come out. I will then kill him in battle and return to Dwaraka.'

statements.claim: Mayavati had trained him in every form of illusion, and he had become expert in the use of all sorts of weapons.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (15-16): Mayavati 'instructed him in all forms of illusion'; Pradyumna 'became an expert in the use of all sorts of weapons.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna strung his bow, took up arrows and struck down the jeweled standard, so that the great pole came down across the gate and the lion emblem lay in the dust.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (end of passage): 'the large-armed Pradyumna stringed his bow, took up arrows and struck down that jewel of a standard.' The fall of the emblem across the gate is scene-setting consistent with the striking-down.

statements.claim: Word of the standard's spoliation reached Shamvara; filled with anger he ordered his hundred sons to go and kill Rukmini's son: 'Go quickly... and kill Rukmini's son.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.251): 'Hearing of the spoliation of his standard... Shamvara, filled with anger, ordered his sons... "do you soon kill Rukshmini's son"'; number confirmed by corpus-chain next title ('Pradyumna Slays the Hundred Sons of Shamvara').

statements.claim: His father Krishna's banner bore the emblem of Garuda and he was mightier than Indra himself.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.251 (Mayavati's speech): 'your father, having the emblem of Garuda on his flag, and more powerful than even Shakra himself.'

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the standard 'seemed to hold up the sky', travelers 'measured the city by it', the pole 'came down across the gate like a falling tree', and 'the silence after the crash was the loudest thing in the city'.
statements.evidence: Descriptive colour around the supported striking-down of the lion standard; no sourceable factual assertion.

notes: Faithful to Harivamsha 1.251: the resolve, the lion-emblazoned jeweled standard standing like Mount Sumeru, the striking-down, and Shamvara's angry dispatch of his sons all match. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: A great hair-stirring encounter took place between Rukmini's son and the sons of Shamvara, who in anger showered on Pradyumna arrows, spears, axes, javelins and maces all at once; Pradyumna, angered, struck each of them with five arrows.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (1-3): 'in anger those great Daityas began to shower simultaneously on Pradyumna arrows, Saktis, Parashwadhas, Tomara's, Kuntas, Bhushundis and maces... Krishna's son too, worked up with anger, struck them in the battle each with five arrows shot off his bow.'

statements.claim: The resolute Asuras set up a net-work of weapons to kill Pradyumna, who killed the ten highly powerful sons of Shamvara.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (4-6): 'those resolute Asuras, exceedingly wroth, set up a net-work of weapons for killing Pradyumna... He then killed the ten highly powerful sons of Shamvara.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna next cut off Chitrasena's head with a broad-headed arrow (bhalla).
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (6): 'the powerful son of Keshava soon cut off Chitrasena's head with a Bhalla.'

statements.claim: The remaining sons of Shamvara united against him, running and shooting arrows, and Pradyumna cut off their heads as if in sport; having thus slain all one hundred sons of Shamvara — all good bowmen — he stood in the battlefield desirous of fighting.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (7-10): 'the remaining sons of Shamvara... began to run taking up and discharging arrows... The highly powerful son of Krishna... cut off their heads, as if in sport. Having thus slain one hundred sons of Shamvara, all good bow men, he stood in the battle field desirous of fighting.'

statements.claim: Hearing of the death of his hundred sons, Shamvara was filled with wrath; he asked his charioteer to get ready his car, and the charioteer saluted him touching the ground with his head, brought the car and asked the soldiers to get ready.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (10-11): 'Hearing of the death of his hundred sons Shamvara was filled with wrath. He asked his charioteer to get ready his car. Receiving the order of the king the charioteer saluted him touching the ground with his head and brought the car there, and asked the soldiers to get ready soon.'

statements.claim: The car was drawn by a thousand bears, tied with ropes of snakes, coated with tiger-skin, adorned with a network of small bells, painted with stars and adorned with gold, with ten stairs, flags bearing the figures of lions, wooden fenders and iron axles, high like the summit of Mount Mandara, bedecked with chowries and golden standards.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (11-16): 'It was drawn by a thousand bear and tied with the ropes of snakes. It was coated with tiger-skin, adorned with a net-work of small bells... It had ten stairs... was painted with stars and adorned with gold. It had a huge standard... embellished with flags having the figures of lions painted on them. It had wooden fenders around it and iron axles. It was high like the summit of Mandara, was bedecked with beautiful chowries... adorned with golden standards.' (The pack additionally says the car was 'filled with wolves', which the story omits — an omission, not a distortion.)

statements.claim: As if urged on by Death, Shamvara, putting on golden armour and taking up his bow and arrows, set out with his soldiers and four ministers — Durdhara, Ketumali, Shatruhanta and Pramardana — and an army of two hundred chariots, ten thousand elephants, eight thousand horses and ten lakh foot soldiers.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (17-22): 'As if urged on by Death, Shamvara, putting on a golden armour and taking up his bow and arrows, set out for battle accompanied by his soldiers and four ministers. Encircled by his ministers, Durdhara, Ketumali, Shatruhanta and Pramarddana... When with two hundred cars, ten thousands elephants, eight thousand horses and ten lakhs of infantry Shamvara set out...'

statements.claim: Portents appeared: cranes uttered hideous yells, firebrands fell, jackals yelled, vultures sat on the standards desirous of the Danavas' blood, headless figures dropped on his car, the moon was eclipsed (possessed by Rahu) and encircled by its disc, his left hand and eye danced, the horses slackened, Indra sent a shower of blood mixed with live coals and cinders, and the reins slipped from the charioteer's hands.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (23-32): 'The cranes began to emit hideous yells... fire-brands... began to fall down. The jackals yelled... vultures sat on the tops of the standards desirous of drinking the blood of the Danavas. Headless figures were seen dropping on his car... The moon was possessed by Rahu (eclipsed) and encircled by its disc. His left hand and eye danced presaging some calamity and the horses... became of slackened speed... Indra began to send down a shower of blood mixed with live coals and cinders... reins slipped off the hands of the charioteer.'

statements.claim: Shamvara, filled with anger, paid no attention to the portents and proceeded to slay Pradyumna; the earth shook at the sound of bugles, conch-shells and drums, and terrified beasts and birds fled; Pradyumna, bent on slaying his enemy, waited in the battlefield.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (32-33): 'But Shamvara, filled with anger, paid no attention to those portends and proceeded for slaying Pradyumna. Thereat the earth shook at the sound of bugles, conch-shells... Overwhelmed with terror... beasts and birds fled away on all sides. Krishna's son, however, bent on slaying his enemy, waited in the battle-field.'

statements.claim: Frame: Pradyumna 'stood untouched among the fallen' and 'the field was quiet except for the wind moving in the fallen flags'.
statements.evidence: The pack says Pradyumna stood 'desirous of fighting' after the slaughter; 'untouched' and the quiet-field image are battlefield atmosphere consistent with the account, which never has the hundred sons wound him.

notes: Dense, faithful rendering of Harivamsha 1.252: five arrows each, ten sons, Chitrasena's head, the hundred bowmen slain, Shamvara's wrath, the full chariot description, the four ministers, army numbers and the omen catalogue all match the Dutt text. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: Shamvara, encircled by soldiers, struck Pradyumna with thousands of arrows; Pradyumna, displaying quick-handedness, cut those arrows off before they could reach him, and bending his bow shot arrows so that there was none in the army who was not struck.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (34-38): 'Shamvara... struck Pradyumna with thousands of arrows. He, however, displaying quick-handedness, cut those arrows off before they could reach him. And bending his bow he shot arrows that there was none in the army who was not struck with one.'

statements.claim: Shamvara's men, assailed, returned to him in fear; beside himself with anger, Shamvara ordered his four ministers — Durdhara, Ketumali, Shatruhanta and Pramardana — 'At my command, go and strike my enemy's son. Do not neglect him; kill him at once. A danger ignored at its beginning grows like a disease — leave this boy alone and he will ruin us all.'
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (38-42): 'Beholding his men take to their heels, Shamvara, beside himself with anger, ordered his ministers. "At my mandate do ye proceed and strike my enemy's son. Do not neglect him but kill him at once. If neglected he will ultimately ruin us like a disease disregarded in the beginning."'

statements.claim: Filled with anger and obeying Shamvara's command, the ministers drove their chariots out showering arrows; Pradyumna, the enhancer of Rukmini's delight, quickly took up his bow and struck Durdhara with twenty-five arrows, Ketumali with sixty-three, Shatruhanta with seventy and Pramardana with eighty-two; the angered ministers then covered him with a downpour of their own arrows.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.252 (43-49): 'Obeying Shamvara's command and filled with anger the ministers drove their cars showering arrows... The highly powerful Pradyumna, the enhancer of the delight of Rukshmini, in anger, struck Durdhara with twenty-five arrows, Ketumali with sixty three, Satruhanta with seventy and Pramarddana with eighty two. Thereat filled with anger the ministers covered Pradyumna with a downpour of arrows.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna shot an arrow at the breast of the short-lived Durdhara and the minister fell; before the eyes of the whole army he cut off Ketumali's head; the heart of the mighty Shatruhanta was cut out; and Pramardana was crushed down with Pradyumna's club.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.252): 'he shot it at the breast of the short-lived Durdhara... with it before all he cut off Ketumali's head... the heart of the highly powerful Shatruhanta was cut off... Kama... crushed down Pramarddana with that club.'

statements.claim: The demon army — which had watched its hundred princes and now its four greatest warriors die — could bear no more: the soldiers fled the field in terror, abandoning their king and banners, and the rout was total.
statements.evidence: The pack's index entry for this event states the outcome as 'Pradyumna slays the four Danava ministers... one by one, and their army flees in terror'; the physical details (weapons thrown down, banners abandoned) are consistent dramatic rendering of that rout.

statements.claim: Frame: his mother was far away in Dwaraka, unaware that the son she had mourned for years was on a field in the demon country; and 'the omens that had darkened Shamvara's march were fulfilled at last'.
statements.evidence: Narrative frame consistent with the pack (mother bewailing like a cow estranged from its calf, HV 1.251; the omen catalogue of HV 1.252); no independent factual assertion.

statements.claim: Scene-setting: the ministers' bodies lay in a ring around Pradyumna with their chariots wrecked and flags trailing in the dirt, and the field emptied 'like a tide going out'.
statements.evidence: The pack confirms the ministers were slain from their cars and the army fled; the specific wrecked-chariot and trailing-flag imagery is descriptive colour beyond the excerpted text.

notes: Faithful to Harivamsha 1.252 (second half): Shamvara's arrow volley, the counter-volley, the command to the ministers, the exact arrow counts (25/63/70/82), and the four distinct deaths (arrow to Durdhara's breast, Ketumali's head, Shatruhanta's heart, Pramardana crushed by club) all match the pack. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.
